```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library("naboer")
```

A fold assesses observations whose predictions contribute to a criterion and
omits observations unavailable during fitting. Assessment is a subset of omission;
the difference contains exclusion-only observations. These may be dependence
buffers, unavailable future observations, or observations outside a sliding
training window. Analysis is the complement of omission. Diagnostics retain the
names `n_buffer` and `buffer_size` for these exclusion-only counts; plots label
them `omitted`.

```{r}
x <- tibble::tibble(time = 1:8, y = c(1, 2, 2, 4, 3, 5, 7, 6))
folds <- custom_folds(x, assessment = list(3L, 6L), omission = list(2:4, 5:7))
tibble::as_tibble(folds, membership = TRUE)
as_nei(folds)
```

`nei$a` concatenates omission indices; `ma` contains cumulative endpoints.
`d` and `md` encode assessment. The first endpoint starts at position one; there
is no leading zero. Repeated assessment across folds is retained, including its
effect on the criterion. No automatic fold weighting is applied.

| Prediction target | Design |
|---|---|
| Baseline prediction among sampled units | LOO or random V-fold, where appropriate for the dependence and target |
| Beyond local residual dependence | Focal neighbourhoods, optionally buffered blocks |
| New locations in the sampled region | Spatial block holdouts |
| New periods | Temporal blocks |
| Future observations | Forecast origins, horizon and gap |
| New groups | Whole-group or hierarchical holdouts |
| New environments | Predictor-space clusters or strata |
| New taxa | Phylogenetic clades, distance blocks or neighbourhoods |

These designs pose different questions. Blocked validation can require
extrapolation in predictors; a large error does not automatically imply a poor
interpolation model. Choose dependence radii using scientific knowledge or
separate diagnostics; naboer does not infer them automatically.

Keys identify repeated series or observational units; they do not declare
independence. Use `.by` only for domains across which generated dependence
queries should never pass. Custom membership and existing exclusions are
retained as supplied. Whole-block V-fold allocation can combine several domains
in one fold; `.by` does not request a separate V-fold schedule per domain.
Observations in other domains remain available for fitting,
including future observations in forecasting designs. If information would not
be available at prediction time, do not declare it to be an independent domain
merely to obtain a particular fold layout.

Blocking in space or time can also separate the training and assessment ranges
of environmental predictors. Match the design to the intended deployment:
interpolation among sampled units, transfer to new units, and extrapolation to
new environments are different estimands. A valid fold design does not ensure
that every training model is identifiable or can predict previously unseen
factor levels. Check those properties for the model and prediction target.

## Model alignment and mgcv

Prepare complete modelling data first. Constructors preserve canonical order.
`fold_data()` returns that order; `as_nei(data = ...)` can check it. With `id`,
alignment checks compare identifiers; otherwise all canonical columns must match.
Rebuild folds after changing observations.

```{r model, eval=requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)}
all_folds <- loo_folds(x)
fit <- mgcv::gam(y ~ s(time, k = 4),
  data = fold_data(all_folds),
  method = "NCV", nei = as_nei(all_folds), na.action = stats::na.fail
)
fit$sp
```

`gam()` supports NCV and QNCV; `bam()` supports NCV with `discrete = TRUE`.
Leave `jackknife` unspecified to preserve mgcv's covariance default. For sampled
bam criteria, keep every neighbourhood and supply `sample` through `as_nei()`.
Discarding unsampled definitions changes the information available for covariance.
For buffered or blocked designs, use at least two explicit sampled fold numbers,
for example `as_nei(all_folds, sample = c(1L, 3L, 5L))`. In the tested mgcv
1.9-4 implementation, scalar counts sample packed endpoints rather than fold
numbers, so naboer rejects that form unless all omission sets are singletons.
Export also requires at least two folds: a single native fold is useful for
inspection or explicit rsample refitting, but the tested `gam()` path rejects it.
The initial integration baseline is mgcv 1.9-4. For `bam()`, NCV is applied to
the working penalised linear model; its score should not be interpreted as an
exact non-Gaussian refit criterion. Large blocked omissions can be particularly
expensive in `bam()`; its NCV path is intended for small neighbourhoods.

## Approximation accuracy and large omissions

A valid design does not guarantee approximation accuracy. Except for quadratic
loss, NCV uses a local approximation to the omitted-data fit. QNCV also
approximates the criterion; it provides a finite criterion where supported, not
a guarantee of agreement with exact refits or of improved accuracy over NCV.
The asymptotic argument in the NCV paper assumes neighbourhood size does not
increase with sample size. Large blocks and forecast omissions need separate
checks rather than an appeal to that small-neighbourhood result.

`benchmarks/approximation.R` compares both criteria with exact refits using the
same full-data basis and fixed smoothing parameter. Rebuilding a smooth basis
on each training subset can change its centring or penalty scaling, confounding
the comparison. With 120 observations, seed 20261017 and smoothing parameter
0.2, Gaussian relative criterion discrepancies were below `3.3e-13`. The
corresponding Poisson stress test gave:

| Temporal radius | Maximum omitted fraction | NCV relative criterion error | QNCV relative criterion error |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 7 | 12.5% | 0.23% | 0.47% |
| 15 | 25.8% | 6.04% | 15.10% |
| 30 | 50.8% | 0.37% | 25.37% |
| 48 | 80.8% | 15.36% | 68.98% |

These are one-fixture results, not accuracy bounds or recommended radii. Errors
need not grow monotonically with window width, and total criterion agreement
can hide differences between individual predictions. The script also records
the largest link-scale prediction discrepancy and checks refit convergence.
It does not test the accuracy of optimised smoothing parameters or interval
coverage. For a scientific application, compare approximate and exact refits on
representative folds and candidate smoothing parameters. Use explicit refitting
through `as_rset()` when the approximation is unsuitable.

See the [mgcv NCV documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/NCV.html)
and [bam documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/bam.html)
for the model-specific interpretation and computational limits.
